cues.en: Cities are a big deal. We pretty much all have to live in them. We should try hard to get them right. So few cities are nice. Very, very few out of many thousands are really beautiful.
cues.zh: 城市非常重要。我们几乎都得住在城市里。我们应该努力把城市建好。可真正宜居的城市太少了。成千上万座城市中，真正称得上美的寥寥无几。

cues.en: Embarrassingly,
cues.zh: 说来难堪，

cues.en: the more appealing ones tend to be old, which is weird because we're mostly much better at making things now. Cars, planes or phones, why not then cities?
cues.zh: 越是有吸引力的城市往往越古老，这很奇怪，因为如今我们制造东西的能力大多强得多。汽车、飞机、手机都越做越好，城市为什么不行呢？

cues.en: It's crazy to settle for this and to leave something so important to chance. We need to get more scientific and identify the principles that determine how a city gets to be pretty or ugly. It's not a mystery why we like some cities so much better than others. This is a manifesto about how to make attractive cities. There are six fundamental things a city needs to get right.
cues.zh: 对现状将就，把如此重要的事交给运气，这太离谱了。我们需要更科学，找出决定城市美丑的原则。我们为什么偏爱某些城市，并非无解之谜。这是一份关于如何打造宜人城市的宣言。一座城市要做好六件根本的事。

cues.en: One of the things we really love in cities is order.
cues.zh: 城市中我们真正喜爱的一点是秩序。

cues.en: Order means balance, symmetry, and repetition. It means the same thing happening again and again and the left side matching the right side. Order is one of the reasons so many people love Paris,
cues.zh: 秩序意味着平衡、对称和重复。意味着同样的事物一遍遍出现，左边与右边相称。秩序是许多人热爱巴黎的原因之一，

cues.en: but most cities are a complete mess.
cues.zh: 但大多数城市却是一片混乱。

cues.en: When it's a mess, it seems like no one's in charge, and that's worrying.
cues.zh: 混乱之时，仿佛无人主事，这令人担忧。

cues.en: It's horrible when everything is jumbled up. A pitched roof next to a flat roof, a stark geometrical box next to a muddled car park, high rise towers that look as if they've been placed at random like teeth in a gaping mouth.
cues.zh: 一切杂乱无章时，那感觉很糟糕。坡屋顶挨着平屋顶，硬朗的几何方盒挨着杂乱的停车场，高层塔楼像是随机插在那里，如同张开的嘴里参差的牙齿。

cues.en: We generally have an itch to straighten things out and when we can't, it's frustrating.
cues.zh: 我们通常总想把事情理顺，如果做不到，就会感到很沮丧。

cues.en: The same urge is there when we look at cities.
cues.zh: 当我们审视城市时，也会产生同样的冲动。

cues.en: Often, it's not skyscrapers
cues.zh: 通常，我们反感的并不是摩天大楼本身，

cues.en: we mined in the city, it's skyscrapers that have been dumped without planning like they are increasingly in London, whereas New York or Chicago shows the ordered way that we love.
cues.zh: 而是城市里缺乏规划、随意堆砌的建筑，就像如今越来越严重的伦敦那样；而纽约或芝加哥展现出的，才真正是我们钟爱的秩序感。

cues.en: However, you have to keep something else in mind. Excessive order can be just as much of a problem. Too much regularity can be soul destroying.
cues.zh: 但我们还必须牢记一点：过度追求秩序同样也是个问题，太死板的规律性甚至会扼杀灵魂。

cues.en: Too much order feels rigid and alien. It can be bleak, relentless, and harsh.
cues.zh: 过度的秩序会让人感到僵化与疏离，显得冷漠、无情且压抑。

cues.en: So the ideal we're seeking is variety
cues.zh: 因此，我们追求的理想境界是多样性

cues.en: and order.
cues.zh: 与秩序的结合。

cues.en: This is the idea in a square in Telch in The Czech Republic where every house is the same width and height, but within that ordered pattern, every house has been allowed freedom at the level of form and color. Or in Java Island in Amsterdam, where the pattern is quite strict, each house is the same height and width, the color range is restricted, but within this grid, each unit is completely individual.
cues.zh: 捷克泰尔奇的广场就体现了这一理念：那里的每座房屋宽度和高度都相同，但在这种规整的格局中，每栋房子在造型和色彩上都享有充分的自由。阿姆斯特丹的爪哇岛（Java Island）也是如此，虽然规整度极高，每栋房子同高同宽、用色受限，但在这种网格格局之下，每个单元都极具个性。

cues.en: We're perfectly in the middle between chaos and boringness here, and that's what humans adore. That's what more and more cities should have, order and variety.
cues.zh: 这种恰好处于混乱与乏味之间的绝妙平衡，正是人们所由衷喜爱的。这也正是越来越多城市应当具备的特质：兼具秩序与多样性。

cues.en: So as a general rule, too much mess and it's off putting, but too much simple order and it's boring.
cues.zh: 因此总的规律是：太杂乱会让人反感，但过于单一的秩序又索然无味。

cues.en: What we crave is organized complexity,
cues.zh: 我们真正渴望的是“有组织的复杂性”，

cues.en: which you can see as much here
cues.zh: 它既体现在这里，

cues.en: as here.
cues.zh: 也同样体现在那里。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: for the second thing that makes cities beautiful. They have to have visible life.
cues.zh: 来看让城市美丽的第二个要素：城市必须展现出鲜活的生活气息。

cues.en: There are streets that are dead and streets that are alive and in general we crave the live ones. This is a live street in Hong Kong.
cues.zh: 有的街道死气沉沉，有的则生机勃勃，而我们普遍都渴望后者。这是一条充满生机的香港街道。

cues.en: This is a live scene in Venice. In the eighteenth century, the painter Canaletto specialized in pictures of cities everyone loved because they're full of life. There's always plenty going on. In this painting, we can see a stonemason's yard. The worksheds are rough, but they're charming. It's fascinating to see what people are up to. How do they load those huge blocks onto the gondolas? The life of the city is on display,
cues.zh: 这是威尼斯生动的一幕。在18世纪，画家 Canaletto 擅长画人人喜爱的城市画作，因为画中洋溢着生活气息。街上总有各种事情在上演。在这幅画里，我们能看到一个石匠工坊。工棚虽简陋却极具魅力。看着人们各忙各的十分引人入胜。他们究竟是怎么把那些大石块搬上贡多拉的？整座城市的生活就这样展现在眼前，

cues.en: and we're primed to love this.
cues.zh: 而我们天生就热爱这种景象。

cues.en: Contrast this with the dead streets of many modern cities.
cues.zh: 反观许多现代城市中那些毫无生气的街道。

cues.en: Today, the places where a lot of the work gets done look dull and dead. They're spaced out along huge highways, and you never go there unless you happen to work there yourself because there's nothing to see.
cues.zh: 如今，许多集中办公的地方看起来既枯燥又沉闷。它们零散分布在宽阔的高速路沿线，除非你刚好在那上班，否则绝不会去，因为根本没什么可看的。

cues.en: And most office buildings are brutally anonymous.
cues.zh: 而且大多数写字楼都极其千篇一律、冷漠无趣。

cues.en: The people inside might be working on all sorts of fascinating stuff but we just don't know and it's disorienting and cold.
cues.zh: 里面的人可能在做着各种有趣的事情，但我们完全不得而知，只让人感到疏离与冰冷。

cues.en: The street levels are dead.
cues.zh: 临街底层一片死寂。

cues.en: Contrast this with the streets we all love where you can see things going on, a bakery, a cobbler's shop, a market selling carpets, a burger bar, a bookshop.
cues.zh: 对比一下大家喜爱的街道，那里总能看到市井百态：面包房、修鞋铺、卖地毯的摊位、汉堡店、书店。

cues.en: These are streets we love because they're full of life.
cues.zh: 我们喜爱这些街道，正是因为它们充满了鲜活的生命力。

cues.en: More and more in modern cities, we've hidden life away.
cues.zh: 在现代城市中，我们越来越多地把生活隐藏起来。

cues.en: We have lots of dead sheds and dead towers connected up by dead motorways where you can barely glimpse your fellow humans.
cues.zh: 我们有许多死寂的棚屋和高塔，由死寂的高速公路连接，你几乎看不到自己的同类。

cues.en: Rather than the old alleyways where you can see people at work, look at them in the eye as they walk down the road and feel connected to others.
cues.zh: 而不是像过去的小巷那样，你能看到人们在劳作，在他们走在路上时与他们目光交汇，感受到与他人的联结。

cues.en: Modern planners have become obsessed by hiding technology rather than trying to make it nice to look at. Today, we'd be outraged if we heard a huge pipeline was gonna be slapped across a lovely river. We'd be up in arms, but we booked trips to go and see the Roman Pont Du Gard in Southern France.
cues.zh: 现代规划者痴迷于隐藏技术，而不是设法让它好看。今天，如果我们听说一条巨大的管道要被横跨在一条美丽的河流上，我们会怒不可遏。我们会强烈抗议，可我们却预订行程去看法国南部的罗马加尔桥。

cues.en: That's because it's built for beauty and practicality.
cues.zh: 那是因为它兼顾了美观与实用。

cues.en: We think it's the pipe we hate, it's not, it's just the ugliness.
cues.zh: 我们以为我们讨厌的是管道，其实不是，我们讨厌的只是丑陋。

cues.en: So let's make sure our streets are full of life, full of people doing stuff you can see through the windows. That's what makes certain cities so attractive to walk along, That work is on show, that people are proud of what they're doing and are happy to let the world notice and appreciate the practical side of things. There's a third principle of good cities. They are compact.
cues.zh: 所以，让我们确保街道充满生机，满是透过窗户就能看到在忙碌的人们。这正是某些城市如此适合漫步的原因——工作在展示，人们为自己的所作所为感到自豪，乐于让世界注意到并欣赏事物实用的一面。好城市的第三条原则是：它们紧凑。

cues.en: In the past, being able to be alone or just with your partner or family was at first a huge achievement. Only the largest class, the poor lived huddled together and it was horrid.
cues.zh: 在过去，能够独处，或只与伴侣、家人在一起，起初是一项巨大的成就。只有最大的阶层——穷人，才挤在一起住，那很可怕。

cues.en: As soon as people had money, they wanted to move out and have their own plots.
cues.zh: 人们一有了钱，就想搬出去，拥有自己的地块。

cues.en: Through the later decades of the twentieth century,
cues.zh: 在二十世纪的后几十年里，

cues.en: more and more people tuck themselves away in a private realm and it's been a disaster.
cues.zh: 越来越多的人把自己藏进私人空间，结果是一场灾难。

cues.en: It's become deadly, cold, boring, and very very wasteful on the environment. A compact city like Barcelona swallows a fraction of the energy of a sprawling one like Phoenix in Arizona.
cues.zh: 它变得致命、冷漠、无聊，而且对环境极其浪费。像巴塞罗那这样紧凑的城市，所消耗的能源只是亚利桑那州凤凰城这类 sprawling 城市的一小部分。

cues.en: We've built a world of endless dead dormitory suburbs connected by sterile wide motorways,
cues.zh: 我们建起了一个由无尽死寂的宿舍式郊区组成的世界，这些郊区被毫无生气的宽阔高速公路连接起来，

cues.en: all because we labor under the false impression that we want to be far away from other people. But in fact, it's wonderful to have the balancing moderating influence of living close to other people in uplifting surroundings.
cues.zh: 这一切都是因为我们误以为自己想远离他人。但事实上，住在能提振心情的环境中、与他人邻近而居，那种平衡而温和的影响是非常美好的。

cues.en: That's why we need tightly packed, well ordered cities with lots of squares and public places in which we can hang out.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们需要紧密排列、秩序井然的城市，里面有大量广场和公共场所供我们消磨时光。

cues.en: All the most beautiful compact cities have squares, yet the art of the square has gone into terrible decline. We keep promoting the invention of mobile phones, but no one's built a good square anywhere on this planet for decades. It's not rocket science though. Look at the Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere Rome. It's a public place, but intimate and enclosed enough to feel like an extension of your home. Lounging about here, having a coffee or a beer, reading a paper, you get to be around other people. Their moderating cheering effect is restoring. It takes you away from the over intense, couple obsessed atmosphere of the home.
cues.zh: 所有最美的紧凑城市都有广场，然而广场的艺术已经严重衰落。我们不断推动手机的发明，但几十年来这个星球上没有任何地方建起过一个好广场。不过这并非火箭科学。看看罗马特拉斯提弗列的圣玛丽亚广场。它是一个公共场所，却足够私密、足够围合，感觉就像你家的延伸。在这里闲坐，喝杯咖啡或啤酒，读份报纸，你就能身处他人之中。他们那种温和、令人振奋的影响具有恢复作用。它把你从家中那种过度紧张、过度专注于伴侣的氛围中带走。

cues.en: There's an art to a good square. It should be neither too big nor too small. Anything over 30 meters in diameter starts to become too large, by which we mean the individual becomes overly small relative to the space around them, creating a sense of alienation and dislocation.
cues.zh: 好的广场是有讲究的。不能太大，也不能太小。直径超过30米就开始太大了，意思是相对于周围的空间，个人显得过于渺小，产生一种疏离和错位感。

cues.en: In a good square, you should be able to see the face of a person across the square. You could, if need be, hail someone walking on the other side. The ideal square must offer a feeling of containment,
cues.zh: 在一个好的广场上，你应该能看清广场对面某个人的脸。必要时，你可以跟走在对面的人打招呼。理想的广场必须给人一种围合感，

cues.en: but not claustrophobia.
cues.zh: 但不能让人感到幽闭恐惧。

cues.en: There's another principle of good cities to do with orientation
cues.zh: 好城市还有另一个原则，跟方向感有关，

cues.en: and mystery.
cues.zh: 也跟神秘感有关。

cues.en: By definition, cities are huge. But the cities that a lot of people love also have lots of little back streets and small lanes where you can feel cozy and get a bit lost. We're drawn to the sense of mystery and enclosure that these streets offer. It's actually lovely to get a bit lost.
cues.zh: 顾名思义，城市是巨大的。但很多人喜爱的城市，也有许多小巷和窄路，让你感到惬意，还能稍微迷个路。我们被这些街道带来的神秘感和围合感所吸引。稍微迷个路其实挺美好的。

cues.en: A warren of alleyways can feel homely and intimate.
cues.zh: 迷宫般的小巷能给人家的感觉和亲密感。

cues.en: At Cartagena in Colombia, the balconies nearly touch across the street. You can see your neighbors having breakfast. You know when they've gone to bed, what time the children do their homework on a Sunday evening. The fact that everyone's a little bit on display a lot of the time tends to make people nicer. They don't shout at each other quite so much. They put flowers on the table more often. We like it, but we forget that we do, and we don't quite know how to ask for it. Modern planners and developers give us maximum privacy because they suppose that's what we all want, and because they insist that cars and lorries, which like a lot more space than people, are the most important things in the world. Of course, we need balance between small streets and big ones. Necessarily, cities are large. We love small streets, but they're a nightmare when you have to go any distance. So the ideal is to have big boulevards, grand wide straight places,
cues.zh: 在哥伦比亚的卡塔赫纳，阳台几乎横跨街道相触。你能看到邻居在吃早餐。你知道他们什么时候上床睡觉，孩子们周日晚几点写作业。每个人大部分时间都多少暴露在别人视线里，这往往让人变得更好。他们不那么大声吵架了。他们更常在桌上摆花。我们喜欢这样，但我们忘了自己喜欢，也不知道该怎么去争取。现代规划者和开发商给我们最大限度的隐私，因为他们以为这就是我们想要的，也因为他们坚持认为汽车和卡车——它们比人需要更多空间——是世界上最重要的东西。当然，我们需要在小街道和大街道之间取得平衡。城市必然很大。我们喜欢小街道，但要出远门时它们就是噩梦。所以理想的状态是既有宽阔的大道、宏伟笔直的大广场，

cues.en: and also little warrens of streets. We need cities that offer us two important pleasures, the pleasures of mystery and the pleasures of orientation.
cues.zh: 也有小小的街巷迷宫。我们需要这样的城市，能给我们两种重要的愉悦：神秘感的愉悦和方向感的愉悦。

cues.en: Let's think about scale now. Modern cities are all about big things. Joseph Campbell once wrote, if you want to see what a society really believes in, look at what the biggest buildings on the horizon are dedicated to. The biggest, most prominent things tell us about the actual rather than the admitted priorities of a society.
cues.zh: 现在来谈谈规模。现代城市里到处都是庞然大物。Joseph Campbell 曾写道，想知道一个社会真正信奉什么，就看看天际线上那些最大的建筑是为谁而建的。那些最宏伟、最显眼的建筑，揭示了一个社会真正看重什么，而不只是它口头上承认的价值。

cues.en: We don't collectively say we worship sports shoe corporations, tax specialists, the oil industry, and pharmaceuticals.
cues.zh: 我们不会公开承认，自己崇拜运动鞋公司、税务顾问、石油产业和制药企业。

cues.en: Our cities, however, tell another story. They're full of enormous towers devoted to just these things. That is a bit depressing.
cues.zh: 但城市讲述着另一番故事。城里到处都是为这些东西而建的巨塔。这多少令人沮丧。

cues.en: As humans, we don't mind things being big per se. We don't mind being humbled so long as the things we're bowing to deserve homage, like a beautiful mosque or a cathedral or a museum.
cues.zh: 作为人类，我们并不介意事物本身很宏大。只要我们敬仰的对象当得起这份敬意，我们不介意在它面前感到渺小，比如一座美丽的清真寺、大教堂或博物馆。

cues.en: But we've allowed our cities to be hijacked by aggressive commercial interests, by towers that honor not God or love or humanity, but pizza corporations and hedge funds.
cues.zh: 但我们任由激进的商业利益劫持了城市。那些高塔纪念的不是上帝、爱或人类，而是披萨公司和对冲基金。

cues.en: They exist because we've made a big dumb collective mistake.
cues.zh: 它们之所以存在，是因为我们犯了一个愚蠢的集体错误。

cues.en: We focused on who owns land, but we don't think about who owns space, who has air rights. And in the end, who has air rights determines what you can see from your window.
cues.zh: 我们只关注土地归谁所有，却没想过空间归谁所有、谁拥有空域权。归根结底，空域权决定了你能从窗户里看到什么。

cues.en: We suggest that the ideal height for any city block is five stories high. No more. Above that, people start to feel small, insignificant, trivial.
cues.zh: 我们认为，任何城市街区的理想高度都是五层楼。不该再高了。超过这个高度，人就会开始觉得自己渺小、无足轻重、微不足道。

cues.en: So we say, cut down those towers and pack everything into five stories. Make it dense, compact, and tight like they do in some parts of Berlin, Amsterdam, London, and Paris, the bits we love. Of course, occasionally, there can be a huge building, but let's keep it for something really special, something all of humanity can love. Towers have to be worthy of their prominence.
cues.zh: 所以，我们要把那些高楼拆掉，把所有东西都压缩到五层楼里。像柏林、阿姆斯特丹、伦敦和巴黎一些我们喜欢的地方那样，建得密集、紧凑、利落。当然，偶尔也可以有一座宏伟建筑，但要把它留给真正特殊、全人类都能喜爱的事物。高楼必须配得上它们的显眼位置。

cues.en: They must be aligned with our best ambitions and long term needs.
cues.zh: 它们必须符合我们最好的抱负和长期需求。

cues.en: Finally, make it local.
cues.zh: 最后，要因地制宜。

cues.en: Some things should be the same everywhere. We don't expect there to be a uniquely Venezuelan telephone or a distinctively Icelandic bicycle, but we don't want buildings to look the same everywhere. It's hugely disappointing when you fly somewhere for hours, land, and feel you could be anywhere.
cues.zh: 有些东西应该处处相同。我们不要求有独特的委内瑞拉电话，或带有鲜明冰岛特色的自行车，但我们不希望建筑在任何地方看起来都一样。飞上几个小时，落地后却觉得自己哪儿都能在，这实在令人失望。

cues.en: The problem isn't just that we'd like a bit of variation for its own sake. Because of climate, history, and social traditions, each society really does have different needs, different strengths and weaknesses.
cues.zh: 问题不只是我们想要一些变化本身。由于气候、历史和社会传统的不同，每个社会确实都有不同的需求，也各有长处和短处。

cues.en: There are many distinct styles of happiness,
cues.zh: 幸福有许多不同的样式，

cues.en: many good and varied ways of conducting collective life. The sameness of cities is a problem because it reveals how far each must be from engaging with a specific character of its own place.
cues.zh: 集体生活也有许多美好而多样的方式。城市千篇一律，是因为它暴露出一个事实：每座城市都离理解自身地方特色还很远。

cues.en: It's like wearing the same clothes in all climates or speaking in exactly the same way irrespective of who you're talking to. Cities need to have strong characters connected to the use of distinctive local materials and forms.
cues.zh: 这就像在所有气候下都穿同样的衣服，或者不管你在和谁说话，都用完全相同的方式表达。城市需要鲜明的个性，并与独特的本地材料和形式相联系。

cues.en: The pale sandstone of Milbury Crescent in Glasgow's South Side is a local material, a medium grained carboniferous blonde sandstone formed when the Scottish landmass lay near the Equator.
cues.zh: 格拉斯哥南区 Milbury Crescent 的淡色砂岩就是一种就地取材的原料，这种中粒石炭纪浅色砂岩，形成于苏格兰陆块还靠近赤道的时期。

cues.en: Or around Cambridge, brick from the local yellowish Gault clay is a major traditional material.
cues.zh: 或者在剑桥一带，用当地偏黄的高特黏土烧制而成的砖，也是一种主要的传统建材。

cues.en: Or think of the way the great Australian architect, Glen Mercutt, found ways to put up buildings that reflected the distinctive character of Australian life.
cues.zh: 又或者想想澳大利亚伟大的建筑师 Glen Mercutt，他是如何通过建筑来展现澳洲独特的生活风貌的。

cues.en: So the law should be, don't make your city from buildings that could be just anywhere.
cues.zh: 所以应当确立一条准则：别把城市建得千篇一律、放在哪儿都行。

cues.en: Find a style of architecture that reflects what makes your location specific.
cues.zh: 去寻找一种能够体现本地独特特质的建筑风格。

cues.en: The obstacles to building beautiful cities are not economic.
cues.zh: 建设美丽城市的阻碍从来都不是经济问题。

cues.en: Collectively, we've got enough money. We face two main problems. Firstly, an intellectual confusion around beauty and secondly, lack of political will.
cues.zh: 从整体上看，我们资金充裕。我们面临的问题主要有两个：一是关于“美”的思想认知混乱，二是缺乏政治意愿。

cues.en: The intellectual confusion is we think no one has a right to say what's beautiful and what's ugly. We get worried about who decides. We think beauty is subjective,
cues.zh: 认知上的混乱在于，我们认为谁都没资格评判美丑。我们担心该由谁来做决定。我们总觉得美是主观的，

cues.en: so surely no one should say anything about it. It's a very understandable qualm, but it's horribly useful to greedy property developers.
cues.zh: 所以谁也不该对此指手画脚。这种顾虑固然情有可原，但却成了贪婪的地产开发商极好的借口。

cues.en: It's such a relief to these people to learn that there is no such thing as beauty. It means they can get away with murder.
cues.zh: 得知“世上本无绝对的美”，这帮人简直如释重负。这意味着他们可以肆无忌惮地胡作非为。

cues.en: We may not agree to the very last point about what a beautiful city is, but we know an ugly one when we see it. No one's ever willingly taken a holiday in Frankfurt On Main or Birmingham, and there are good reasons for this to do with an objective sense of beauty. So let's stop being dangerously relativistic about this. Yes, there is such a thing as beauty. Sydney and San Francisco and Bath and Bordeaux have it and most other places don't. The proof lies in the tourist statistics.
cues.zh: 对于什么样的城市才算美，我们或许无法达成百分百的共识，但一座城市丑不丑，大家一眼就能看出来。从没人会自愿去美因河畔法兰克福或者伯明翰度假，这背后显然关乎某种对美的客观感知。所以，别再搞这种危险的相对主义了。没错，美是真实存在的。悉尼、旧金山、巴斯和波尔多拥有这种美，而大多数其他地方却没有。旅游业的数据就是最好的证明。

cues.en: Let's not keep saying beauty is just in the eye of the beholder. That's just a gift to the next wealthy idiot who wants to put up a horrible tower.
cues.zh: 别再说美只是观者眼中之事了。那等于送给下一个想盖丑塔的有钱傻瓜一份大礼。

cues.en: The other obstacle is a lack of political will. We've abandoned the design of cities to the greedy rich. We've given up believing in democracy. We face and have lost the battle between the public good and commercial opportunism.
cues.zh: 另一个障碍是缺乏政治意愿。我们把城市设计拱手让给贪婪的富人，放弃了相信民主。在公共利益与商业投机之间，我们正面对这场战斗，而且已经输了。

cues.en: There will always be a greedy slick lobby fighting for ugly development, but we can say no. Beautiful cities have only ever been created when governments impose strict and ambitious regulations to keep the greedy private guys in check.
cues.zh: 总会有圆滑贪婪的游说集团为丑陋开发项目奔走，但我们可以说不。只有政府施加严格而雄心勃勃的监管，约束贪婪的私人开发商，美丽的城市才曾被创造出来。

cues.en: Think of Edinburgh's amazing new town, which only got off the ground because the government established clear rules to keep developers in check. They wrote precise legislation detailing heights of buildings, quality of finish, the width of pavements, and the character of the skyline.
cues.zh: 想想爱丁堡令人惊叹的新城，它之所以能启动，正是因为政府制定了明确规则来约束开发商。他们写下了精确的法规，详细规定建筑高度、完工质量、人行道宽度和天际线特征。

cues.en: That's the only way you get beauty. They didn't leave it to the free market. Do that and you will have chaos. When governments give up on beauty, people start to hate all building. We become collectively despondent.
cues.zh: 这是获得美的唯一方式。他们没有把它交给自由市场。交给自由市场，你只会得到混乱。当政府放弃美，人们就开始讨厌所有建筑。我们会集体变得沮丧。

cues.en: We think we hate all building and that we can't create beautiful places. We get obsessed by restoration and opposed anything new which is wrong because we need places to live. Humanity hasn't put up a single beautiful city since about nineteen o five. When Venice was built, no one regretted the lagoons that had been swallowed up.
cues.zh: 我们以为自己讨厌所有建筑，也以为自己造不出美丽的地方。我们痴迷于修复，反对任何新东西——这是错的，因为我们需要住的地方。人类大约自1905年以来就没建成过一座美丽的城市。威尼斯建成时，没人惋惜那些被吞掉的泻湖。

cues.en: The goal of building should be to put up things that don't leave us regretting the nature that's been lost because the architecture is every bit the equal of the designs of nature.
cues.zh: 建筑的目标，应该是创造出不会让我们为失去的自然感到遗憾的事物，因为建筑本身完全可以与自然的设计相媲美。

cues.en: We can create more beautiful cities, but we have to confront opportunistic developers and our own intellectual confusions.
cues.zh: 我们能打造更美丽的城市，但必须直面投机取巧的开发商，也要克服自身的思想混乱。

cues.en: Governments can only create beauty if they have enough public backing. Political will is ultimately about what all of us, the electorate, are asking for. That's why we made this film and hope to awaken you to your power as citizens to help legislate for beautiful cities in the future. These are the six rules. Now it's time to fight to put them in action.
cues.zh: 政府只有得到足够的公众支持，才能创造美。政治意愿归根结底取决于我们全体选民的诉求。这就是我们拍这部影片的原因，也希望借此唤醒你作为公民的力量，让你推动立法，创造未来的美丽城市。这就是六条规则。现在，该行动起来，让它们付诸实践了。
